sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Prince George's County
sections.html:
Recording takes two stops in person. The county Office of Finance in Largo comes first, then the Land Records Division of the Circuit Court in Upper Marlboro. The Finance step has to be done before the court will take the deed.

  • Step 1, Office of Finance: 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo; 301-952-4030; 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays.
  • Step 2, Land Records Division: 14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, Upper Marlboro; 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays.

Bring the original deed, one full copy, and the State of Maryland land instrument intake sheet. A deed that claims an exemption from recording fees or state transfer tax has to cite every applicable code section from the Maryland Annotated Code. The Land Records Division answers at 301-780-2253, and the courthouse main line is 301-952-3655.

An instrument of 1 to 9 pages costs $20, and that fee covers every page when the instrument concerns a principal residence. A $40 surcharge sits on top for recorded documents. For the current amount, call the Land Records Division at 301-780-2253 before you record.

Payment is due when the document is recorded. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit cards, with checks and money orders payable to The Clerk of the Circuit Court. Documents come back by mail when you supply a return address, and otherwise they wait for pickup.

Three taxes can apply to a sale. The county transfer tax is 1.4%, set under County Code sections 10-187 and 10-188. The state recordation tax is $5.50 per $1,000 of consideration, and the county's Finance Affidavit instructions express the same figure as $2.75 per $500, rounded up to the next $500. The state transfer tax is 0.5%, or 0.25% for a qualifying first-time buyer, under Tax-Property 13-203.

Questions about the state transfer tax go to the Land Records Division. Questions about county transfer and recordation tax go to the Office of Finance. Because the county transfer tax alone is a sizable line item, settle in the contract who pays it. Maryland's default is an equal split unless the contract or a law says otherwise.

The Finance Affidavit is the form Prince George's County uses to claim an exemption from the county transfer tax or the state recordation tax. Every instrument recorded in the county's land records is taxable unless Maryland's code or the county code exempts it, and the affidavit is how a filer names the exemption.

Most of its clauses concern loans and refinances:

  • Clause A: a principal residence refinance, where recordation tax applies to the difference between the new loan and the unpaid principal balance.
  • Clause B-1: a principal residence with a purchase money deed of trust recorded for more than 12 months, covering new loans, modifications and home equity lines.
  • Clause B-2: a refinance by a borrower who does not qualify for B-1, paired with Clause A.
  • Clause C: a refinance of a non-principal residence or investment property, where the 1.4% county transfer tax applies to the difference between the new and original loan amounts.

The property must be the borrower's principal residence in state assessment records. Call the county Treasury for submission details.

sections.h2: Disclosures Maryland requires for Prince George's County sales
sections.html:
Prince George's County has its own line items in the state's residential contract statute. Section 14-117 of the Real Property Article requires, where deferred private water and sewer assessments are recorded, that the contract disclose eight items, including the assessment amount, remaining payments, interest rate, payoff amount, and that prepayment carries no penalty. Those assessments cannot be amortized over more than 20 years.

The contract must also disclose whether a development impact fee was imposed on the property, the total amount, and any unpaid balance. Statewide, every residential sale needs a homestead property tax credit statement, and one- or two-unit contracts need the statement that recordation and transfer taxes are shared equally unless negotiated otherwise.

sections.h2: Property tax and tax sale facts for sellers
sections.html:
The county real property rate is $1.0000 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal 2026, with the state adding $0.1120 and Park and Planning adding $0.2940. Unpaid taxes can lead to a lien sold at the annual tax sale on the second Monday in May.

The county caps the taxable assessment increase for fiscal 2026 at 3%, while the state cap is 10% after the first full tax year. The county's Homeowner Protection Program may keep a limited-income home out of tax sale for at least three years, though enrollment is limited.

If the house you are selling has unpaid taxes, pay the balance from the closing proceeds, or ask the Treasury for a payoff before the May sale date.

Sort the paperwork before the closing date. Confirm who pays the county transfer tax, check whether the contract carries the water and sewer or impact fee disclosures, and ask the title company whether it will make the two trips or send a courier. Bring the signed deed, the intake sheet and the Finance Affidavit if an exemption applies, and carry a check made out to The Clerk of the Circuit Court.

After recording, ask for the deed back by mail or pick it up at the counter. The county shows recorded and verified land records online at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, so you can search for your deed later. Clerks cannot give legal advice or run title searches, so questions about the deed's wording belong with your attorney or title company. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, but the recording steps and taxes are the same.

Prince George's County borders Washington, D.C. on its west side and had 967,201 residents in the 2020 census, making it the second-most populous county in Maryland. Upper Marlboro is the county seat, and Bowie is the largest city. Large unincorporated communities include Largo, Clinton, Oxon Hill, Fort Washington and National Harbor. Metro, MARC and the nearby airports make the county easy to reach, which helps showings.

faqs.q: Where is the Prince George's County land records office?
faqs.a: The Land Records Division is in the Judiciary Administrative Services Building at 14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, in Upper Marlboro. It is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Do I pay the county first or the court first?
faqs.a: The county Office of Finance in Largo comes first, then the Land Records Division in Upper Marlboro. Call 301-952-4030 for the Finance step.

faqs.q: What is the Prince George's County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: It is 1.4% under County Code 10-187 and 10-188. The state also charges a 0.5% transfer tax and a recordation tax of $5.50 per $1,000.

faqs.q: Can I search Prince George's County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the Land Records Online Search at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, which shows recorded and verified land records volumes. Clerks cannot give legal advice or run title searches.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed?
faqs.a: An instrument of 1 to 9 pages is $20, covering every page for a principal residence, plus a $40 surcharge on recorded documents. Call 301-780-2253 to confirm the current amount before you record.
